questions.q: Why can a fit human outrun a horse over a marathon on a hot day?
a: We sweat efficiently and can breathe at whatever rate we need
Our legs are longer and stronger than a horse's
We store more sugar than other mammals do
Our hearts beat faster during long races
questions.why: Most mammals cannot sweat, so they overheat and must stop sooner.

questions.q: What role does the Achilles tendon play in running, according to the summary?
a: It stores energy as it stretches and releases it to propel us
It cushions the foot from hard impacts on the ground
It keeps the foot from rolling inward while running
It pumps extra blood to the lower legs
questions.why: This lets humans use less energy per step than other animals.

questions.q: How do modern running shoes weaken the foot?
a: They act like a cast, limiting movement and weakening muscles
They force the foot to roll outward too far
They make the foot strike the ground too hard
They reduce the amount of oxygen reaching the toes
questions.why: The summary compares a shoe to a plaster cast that leaves foot muscles weaker.

questions.q: What did shoe makers blame for runner's knee, despite few people needing support?
a: The foot's natural inward roll, called pronation
A weak Achilles tendon
Running on hard pavement
Tight calf muscles
questions.why: Only about 3 percent of people have a medical need for pronation shoes.

questions.q: What pacing strategy does the summary recommend for long distances?
a: Run just below your aerobic threshold to burn fat
Sprint early and hold on as long as possible
Keep your heart rate at its maximum
Alternate fast and slow miles in a fixed pattern
questions.why: Staying below the point of heavy breathing lets you use fat instead of limited sugar.
